facts.fact: Google Business Profile is free to claim and maintain, according to the vendor's guide.
facts.quote: It's free, and it determines whether you appear when people search for businesses like yours nearby.

facts.fact: According to the guide, search advertising (Google Ads) lets new businesses pay only when someone clicks, and they can start with any budget.
facts.quote: Pay only when someone clicks

facts.fact: According to the guide, social advertising allows new businesses to start with small budgets.
facts.quote: Start with small budgets

facts.fact: The guide names NBC, Hulu, and ESPN as examples of premium networks where streaming TV advertising places a business's ads.
facts.quote: puts your business on premium networks like NBC, Hulu, and ESPN

facts.fact: The guide's recommended strategy begins with a Phase 1 foundation-building period lasting one month, focused on free tactics.
facts.quote: Phase 1: Build Your Foundation (Month 1)

facts.fact: The guide describes local print and radio advertising as expensive relative to reach for new businesses.
facts.quote: Expensive relative to reach

facts.fact: The guide was published on February 7, 2026.
AdWave advises starting Google Ads at $10-20 per day for a new business and optimizing based on results.
facts.quote: Start small ($10-20/day) and optimize based on results

facts.fact: AdWave's suggested budget for search ads in Phase 2 (months 2-3) of a new business's advertising plan is $300-600 per month.
facts.quote: Budget: $300-600/month on search ads.

facts.fact: AdWave's suggested total advertising budget across channels in Phase 3 (month 4 onward) is $500-1,000 per month.
facts.quote: Budget: $500-1,000/month total across channels.

facts.fact: AdWave states that a new business can start streaming TV advertising at $30 per day to test the channel.
facts.quote: [Start with just $30 a day](https://adwave.com/try-free) to test the channel

facts.fact: AdWave states its streaming TV advertising starts at $30 per day on streaming platforms.
facts.quote: reach local customers on streaming platforms, starting at just $30 a day.

facts.fact: AdWave suggests a new business can add streaming TV advertising to build brand awareness when investing $150-300 per month.
facts.quote: Add streaming TV advertising when you can invest $150-300/month to build brand awareness

facts.fact: The AdWave article cites a common guideline that new businesses spend 7-12% of revenue on advertising, higher than established businesses; this figure is not attributed to a named source.
facts.quote: A common guideline is 7-12% of revenue for new businesses

facts.fact: AdWave suggests advertisers generally aim for at least $3-4 in revenue for every $1 spent on advertising (ROAS).
facts.quote: generally you want at least $3-4 in revenue for every $1 spent.

facts.fact: AdWave says brand-building advertising like TV typically shows meaningful results after 2-3 months of consistent presence.
facts.quote: Brand-building advertising like TV typically shows meaningful results after 2-3 months of consistent presence.

facts.fact: AdWave's timeline for the first phase of a new business's advertising plan has no advertising spend, with cost being time only.
facts.quote: Cost: Time only. No advertising spend yet.

facts.fact: AdWave's plan places the capture-existing-demand phase (search ads) in months 2-3 of a new business's advertising timeline.
facts.quote: ### Phase 2: Capture Existing Demand (Months 2-3)

facts.fact: AdWave's plan places the brand awareness phase (streaming TV and social) starting in month 4 of a new business's advertising timeline.
facts.quote: ### Phase 3: Build Brand Awareness (Month 4+)

facts.fact: AdWave's plan places the scale-what-works phase starting in month 6 of a new business's advertising timeline.
facts.quote: ### Phase 4: Scale What Works (Month 6+)
